text.p: Transport Minister David Anderson voiced approval of tough measures struggling Canadian Airlines Corp announced on Friday, saying Canada needed to continue to have two viable air carriers.
"The measures they intend to take...seem to me to be important, very important indeed," he told reporters.

"We regard the viability of Canadian International and Air Canada, which is also an airline which is not making as much money as some others, we regard this as particularly important. We have a two-airline policy. We want both of them there. We want competition and we want to have low fares...."
"So obviously we're very interested in what's taking place at Canadian," Anderson added, speaking after the airline said continued losses threatened its viability.
The company, in which AMR Corp has a minority share, proposed eliminating up to 250 jobs and cutting wages by 10 percent.
He said Canadian had not asked him for financial assistance or loan forgiveness.
"We've had no request nor do we have the situation which would indicate that that request is about to come to us," Anderson said.

Asked what would happen if the union refused the wage cuts, he said Canadian would make its decisions. "Similarly the union has to recognize the situation that the airline faces and adjust its approach accordingly," he said, adding it was not for him to advise either side how to act.
